QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_31

question.text: Which metric is the PRIMARY performance measure used in GIPS-compliant reporting of open-ended Cat III AIF performance to investors?

explanation.text: The Logic: GIPS mandates TWR (Time-Weighted Return) as the primary metric because it neutralises the effect of investor cash flows and measures pure manager skill. For Cat III (open-ended, daily NAV), TWR is the industry standard. The Trap: IRR/MOIC are Cat I/II PE metrics (XIX-D primary). MWR shows investor-specific return, not manager skill. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D primary metrics are IRR/MOIC; XIX-E primary is TWR. This split is a key exam boundary. Manager's Pro-Tip: Publish BOTH gross and net TWR to LPs in monthly factsheets. Net TWR must reflect all fees including equalisation debits/credits — a common audit finding is stale gross-to-net.
